transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-15 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Sofia Mendes (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (CardinalCare VP Eng), Liam O'Connor (Head of ML Ops), Sanjay Rao (Procurement)
Links shared: Slides: https://bit.ly/redwood-cardinalcare, Benchmark template: drive.google.com/cardinal-bench

00:00 - Jordan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick agenda, want to align on the retainer numbers, confirm regions, and scope a small perf smoke to validate latency targets.
00:28 - Maya Patel: Yep, thanks. Short on time today so we'll try to be crisp. we want to keep the current throughput but shave latency at p95, and also look at rolling out to ap-southeast.
00:45 - Sofia Mendes: Great. quick clarification — when you say p95, are we targeting under 120ms for generation calls or the full chat path including function calls?
01:12 - Liam O'Connor: Ideally the chat end-to-end, but we can be pragmatic: token gen under 80ms is the true blocker for us. the orchestration adds another 30-40ms.
01:35 - Jordan Park: makes sense. ok — high level: we've got three levers here — dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs), geo-activation for ap-southeast, and optional private V-P-C deployment for sensitive workloads.
01:56 - Maya Patel: Private VPC is a likely ask for some PHI traffic. what does that actually mean for onboarding time?
02:10 - Sofia Mendes: In our experience a V-P-C private control plane takes about 6-8 weeks for full activation if there's a standard onboarding (entitlements, K-M-S key exchange, firewalls), could be faster with their infra team aligned. on the perf side, the runtime is the same CUD A optimized path.
02:40 - Liam O'Connor: quick interjection — are you supporting customer-managed KMS or only Redwood KMS?
02:50 - Jordan Park: we support both. can do customer-managed K-M-S or Redwood-managed keys; we document H-S-M patterns for airgapped cases as well.
03:05 - (Speaker 1): uh-huh.
03:18 - Sofia Mendes: for the retainer numbers we modeled two SKUs: Reserved-Standard (3x A100-equivalent) and Reserved-Plus (6x, includes burst). We can share the SKU table after this call.
03:39 - Maya Patel: good. what's the SLA delta between reserved and hosted?
03:50 - Jordan Park: reserved capacity comes with a 99.9% uptime SLA and a latency SLO at the model route level; hosted is best-effort with regional fallback. reserved also gives you guaranteed throughput and isolation which seems important for you.
04:15 - Sanjay Rao: From procurement's POV we need the contract amendment language — we're fine with the price, but need a clause around data retention and audit logs. do you provide per-token audit trails?
04:34 - Sofia Mendes: yes, we provide full request/response audit logs at the token route level, and you can toggle retention windows. we'll include the SOC two report and audit log spec.
04:50 - Liam O'Connor: any gotchas with prefix KV caching and can we evict per-namespace? we rely on KV cache aggressively for chat.
05:03 - Sofia Mendes: yep you can control cache TTLs per-namespace, can do evicts. small note — the KV cache sometimes shows as K-V case in auto transcripts.
05:18 - Maya Patel: (laughs) noted.
05:28 - Jordan Park: let's talk regions — you asked for ap-southeast region activation. two paths: 1) enable hosted region with our standard images, 2) provision a private geocluster (private nodes + VPC peering). hosted region is fastest — typically 10 business days. private geocluster is 4-6 weeks.
05:58 - Liam O'Connor: latency target for ap-southeast users is 150ms p95 for short prompts, currently hitting 260ms. is there an intermediate option?
06:15 - Sofia Mendes: we can do a hybrid: edge routing to closest hosted region plus prefix caching. That usually buys ~60-80ms. also quantization and reduced context size helps.
06:35 - Maya Patel: speak to cost — hybrid seems cheaper than private nodes. procurement will push for hosted unless compliance blocks it.
06:48 - Sanjay Rao: correct. If we can keep PHI in a private cluster and route non-PHI to hosted, that could be acceptable. need to validate the line between them.
07:02 - Jordan Park: exactly — recommended architecture: private VPC for PHI routes (pinned model variant) + hosted for general traffic. we'll diagram that in the topo doc.
07:20 - (00:07:20) Sofia Mendes: technical deep dive — when we run the perf smoke we should test with your peak qps, 99th token length distribution, and function calling turned on. that reveals kernel selection behavior.
07:40 - Liam O'Connor: we can supply a 2-hour sample trace from prod with masked data. would you run it in your staging and attach results?
07:54 - Sofia Mendes: yes, small caveat — we'll run in staging with similar hardware and approximate sequence lengths; results will be indicative but not canonical. we'll capture traces and token-level latencies.
08:12 - Maya Patel: what about fallback policies? if ap-southeast goes down do requests failover to us-west? what's the impact on latency and cost?
08:25 - Jordan Park: failover to us-west is automatic if you allow cross-region fallback; latency will increase and cost may be slightly higher due to cross-region egress. we can set routing policy to prefer regional variants and disable fallback for sensitive routes.
08:48 - Sanjay Rao: legal wants to see the egress numbers; can you provide an estimate for cross-region fallback egress per month for our baseline?
09:00 - Jordan Park: we can approximate once you give us monthly token volumes per region. action item: Liam share token volumes.
09:12 - (00:09:12) Maya Patel: timeline — we'd like a contractual amendment by end of month, ideally live in ap-southeast in Q1. procurement window is 3-4 weeks.
09:27 - Jordan Park: reasonable. on the contract amendment we typically do a one-page amendment to the master subscription with the new SKUs and activation schedule.
09:38 - (Speaker 2): um, quick question — what's the rollback plan if private geocluster underperforms?
09:45 - Sofia Mendes: we keep canary traffic and A/B rollouts; automatic fallback to hosted model variants if the private cluster crosses error/latency thresholds. we also keep a warmed model in hosted as a hot spare.
10:05 - Liam O'Connor: any required infra changes on our side for private? VPC peering, routes, SAML?
10:15 - Jordan Park: VPC peering and a few firewall rules, SAML/SSO for console access, and certificate exchange for mutual TLS. we'll supply a checklist.
10:28 - Maya Patel: security — SOC two and ISO talk? we need SOC two plus pen tests and any compliance attestations.
10:40 - Sofia Mendes: we will share SOC2 Type II and our pen test summary, plus the standard attestation. for deeper audits we have an enterprise package.
10:55 - Sanjay Rao: procurement needs billing terms — monthly invoice or net-30?
11:02 - Jordan Park: standard is net-30 but we can do monthly invoicing and a PO flow — we'll include payment terms in amendment draft.
11:14 - (00:11:14) Sofia Mendes: technical note — for the perf run I'll test two model configs: qp_small (quantized) and qp_full (float) to show tradeoffs between latency and quality.
11:30 - Liam O'Connor: would like to see hallucination delta with quantized path. that's key for our triage team.
11:40 - Sofia Mendes: we can also run a small eval set during the smoke to surface regression metrics.
11:52 - Maya Patel: ok, let's map next steps. can we do a quick readout of expected costs?
12:00 - Jordan Park: I'll send a cost breakdown showing reserved vs hosted vs hybrid for your monthly tokens, plus the amortized cost of private geocluster.
12:12 - Sanjay Rao: any discounts for multi-region commit?
12:18 - Jordan Park: yes — tiered discounts for committed monthly token volumes and multi-region commitments; I'll include a 90-day and 12-month price ladder.
12:30 - (00:12:30) Sofia Mendes: also note the Optimize recommendations — batching, prefix caching settings, and a quantization profile that was helpful for a similar customer — we'll attach those.
12:45 - Maya Patel: good. one more question — who will be the primary SE for the pilot?
12:52 - Jordan Park: Sofia will lead the pilot; I'll be your contract owner.
13:02 - Liam O'Connor: great. we'll get the sample trace to Sofia by Monday. you said the smoke would be by 11/22?
13:10 - Sofia Mendes: yes that's the plan unless there's infra blockers.
13:20 - Jordan Park: wrap up — I'll push pricing + SKUs and SOC2/docs by EOD Thursday, Sofia runs perf and shares CSV by next Monday 11/22, Maya to confirm procurement cadence by 11/20.
13:35 - Maya Patel: sounds good. thanks everyone.
13:42 - (Outro) Jordan Park: thanks — slides and bench template in chat. we'll follow up in CRM.

Notes / transcript quality: medium — occasional mislabels (Speaker 1/2) and some acronyms garbled (KMS -> K-M-S, SOC2 -> Soc two). Natural speech, interruptions, and tradeoffs discussed (latency vs cost, hosted vs private).

End of transcript.
